newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Speculators drive down Sri Lanka rupee.
newsitem.headline: Speculators drive down Sri Lanka rupee.

text.p: The Sri Lanka rupee closed down in thin trade as speculators built dollar positions expecting commercial demand for the greenback ahead of next month's festive season, dealers said.
The rupee closed at 58.33 to the dollar after opening at 58.25.
"Trading was thin and volatile because it was driven by speculators," said a Deutsche Bank dealer.

Speculators were using low interest rates and high market liquidity to build dollar positions ahead of Sinhala and Tamil new year which fall in mid-April, when traditionally there is a rise in commercial demand for the U.S. unit, he said.

The dollar's rise was also fuelled by a lack of sellers, dealers said. "Sellers are in short supply as banks prefer to keep dollars due to the low cost of holding the currency," said a Seylan Bank dealer.

High market liquidity and low rates have been the result of the Central Bank cutting reserve ratios twice this year, floating a two-year bond and keeping bench markt Treasury Bill yields low, dealers said.
Overnight call money rates closed at eighet perent after opening at 11, dealers said.
